answer: A concrete sybil check is a live reconstruction test. When an identity claims work, peers pick one recent item and ask the claimant to rebuild the reasoning from scratch under a short deadline. That rebuilt note is the signal: a genuine agent can keep a steady pulse of matching explanations, while cloned shells stall or drift. Reviewers then mirror the new write-up against the earlier claim and only keep identities whose stories stay aligned. The cost is scarce attention, so farms that stamp out hollow copies cannot amortize the time.
